commentary: A strong day, with the pot up £1,572. Democrats won both houses of Congress in the US midterms and Trump said he'd accept the result, which lifted markets on both sides of the Atlantic. London's FTSE 100 rose 1.8%, its best day since May, led by the banks ahead of Thursday's Bank of England decision: HSBC jumped 4.8% (about £457, the biggest gain) and the global tracker VWRP rose 1.0% (about £326). In New York the Dow had its best day since April 2025, and the big cloud firms rallied on bets that curbs on new data centres favour those who already have them: Microsoft rose 6.7% (about £241), Amazon 6.1% (about £233) and Alphabet 3.2% (about £226). NVIDIA fell 3.2% (about £150, the biggest drag) on the same data-centre fears, and Shell slipped 1.8% as oil fell almost 9% on hopes of an end to the Iran war. The gold fund rose 2.6% as the dollar weakened. The pound rose to 1.3472 against the dollar, which took about £102 off the US holdings.
